issues.legal_issue: A transfer for consideration of property represented as a present transferable interest can attach to the transferor’s later-acquired title even when the transferor initially held only an expectation of succession.
material_facts: The vendors sold the disputed properties for consideration and represented in the sale deed that they were presently entitled to them as reversioners.
The purchaser took the transfer in reliance on that representation.
The vendors had only an expectation of succession when they transferred the properties, but a vendor later acquired title when the life interest ended.
The purchaser’s transfer remained in force, and a later release of an interest to the appellant occurred after the purchaser had acquired title.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was entitled to the benefit of section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, and the transfer attached to the title later acquired by the vendor; the subsequent release did not confer title on the appellant.
issues.legal_principle: Section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act applies when a person fraudulently or erroneously represents that they have authority to transfer property, transfers it for consideration, and the transferee acts on that representation; if the transferor later acquires an interest while the transfer remains in force, the transferee may claim that interest. The transferor’s good or bad faith is immaterial; actual reliance by the transferee is material. The principle applies whether the initial defect is absence of any interest or possession only of an expectant heir’s interest. This accords with Alamanaya Kunigari Nabi Sab v. Murukuti Papiah, Shyam Narain v. Mangal Prasad, Vithabai v. Malhar Shankar, Ram Japan v. Jagesara Kuer, and Syed Bismilla v. Manulal Chabildas; the contrary view in Official Assignee, Madras v. Sampath Naidu and Bindeshwari Singh v. Har Narain Singh was disapproved.

rule.if: property_transfer_dispute and transferor_claimed_present_transferable_interest and transferor_had_only_expected_inheritance and transferee_paid_value and transferee_relied_on_claim and transfer_remained_in_force and transferor_later_acquired_title

predicates.property_transfer_dispute: The dispute concerns a transfer of property and competing claims to title under that transfer.
predicates.transferor_claimed_present_transferable_: The transferor represented that they had a present interest in the property and authority to transfer it.
predicates.transferor_had_only_expected_inheritance: At the time of transfer, the transferor had only an expectation of inheriting the property.
predicates.transferee_paid_value: The transferee gave consideration for the transfer.
predicates.transferee_relied_on_claim: The transferee acted on the transferor’s representation when taking the transfer.
predicates.transfer_remained_in_force: The transfer had not been rescinded, cancelled, or otherwise brought to an end before the later title arose.
predicates.transferor_later_acquired_title: The transferor acquired an interest in the property after making the transfer.

issues.definition: When a property transfer for value is made on a relied-upon claim of present entitlement, remains in force, and the transferor later acquires title despite initially having only an inheritance expectation, the earlier transferee can claim that later-acquired title.

issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on transferring a mere expectation of succession does not prevent a transferee from relying on the statutory rule concerning a representation of present title and later-acquired title.
material_facts: The vendors’ deed described their interest as a present entitlement, although they had only an expectation of succession when they transferred the property.
The purchaser paid consideration and acted on the representation of present entitlement.
A vendor later acquired title, and the competing claim relied on the rule prohibiting transfer of a mere expectation of succession.
issues.conclusion: The prohibition on transferring an expectation of succession did not defeat the purchaser’s claim under section 43; the two provisions operate in different fields, and the purchaser’s plea was under, not against, the statute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(a) of the Transfer of Property Act prohibits a simple transfer of a mere possibility such as an heir apparent’s chance of succession. Section 43 addresses a transfer made on a representation of present authority and operates on an interest later acquired by the transferor. The former is a rule of substantive law and the latter a rule of estoppel; they have different conditions and can each operate according to their terms. Where the transferee knew that the transferor lacked the represented title, the transferee could not have acted on the representation. The distinction between a purported transfer of the chance of succession and a representation of present entitlement is reflected in Alamanaya Kunigari Nabi Sab v. Murukuti Papiah; Official Assignee, Madras v. Sampath Naidu was held erroneous. Decisions concerning contracts to transfer an expectancy, including Sri Jagannada Raju v. Sri Rajah Prasada Rao and Ananda Mohan Roy v. Gour Mohan Mullick, did not resolve the different question of a transferee acting on a representation of present interest.

rule.if: transfer_conflict_case and transferor_claimed_present_transferable_interest and transferor_had_only_expected_inheritance and transferee_paid_value and transferee_relied_on_claim and transferor_later_acquired_title

predicates.transfer_conflict_case: The dispute concerns whether a transfer based on a representation of present entitlement can operate despite a rule against transferring a mere expectation of succession.
predicates.transferor_claimed_present_transferable_: The transferor represented that they had a present interest in the property and authority to transfer it.
predicates.transferor_had_only_expected_inheritance: At the time of transfer, the transferor had only an expectation of inheriting the property.
predicates.transferee_paid_value: The transferee gave consideration for the transfer.
predicates.transferee_relied_on_claim: The transferee acted on the transferor’s representation when taking the transfer.
predicates.transferor_later_acquired_title: The transferor acquired an interest in the property after making the transfer.

issues.definition: Where a transferor represents present entitlement despite having only an inheritance expectation, and a transferee pays value and relies on that representation before the transferor later acquires title, the rule against transferring an expectancy does not defeat the later-acquired-title rule.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory illustration may guide the interpretation of a provision when the provision’s language is broad enough to cover the situation illustrated.
material_facts: The illustration to the provision described a person who sold property represented as transferable although it had been retained by another person, and who later acquired it by inheritance.
The appellant argued that the illustration conflicted with the provision and should be rejected.
The Court concluded that the provision’s language was general enough to cover the transfer described in the illustration.
issues.conclusion: The illustration was relevant and could be used to confirm that the provision covered the transfer; it could not enlarge the provision if the text clearly excluded the situation, but it was not to be rejected as repugnant where the text was broad enough.
issues.legal_principle: An illustration is not part of the statutory text, but it is furnished to assist in applying and construing the provision. It should be accepted as relevant and valuable if it can be reconciled with the text, and should not be rejected as repugnant without a very special case. An illustration cannot enlarge a provision whose clear language excludes the matter. The Court relied on Mahomed Syedol Ariffin v. Yeoh Ooi Gark and referred to Vickers v. Evans on the rule against reading words into a statute without sufficient basis in its text.

predicates.statutory_interpretation_case: The dispute requires the court to determine the scope of statutory language with the aid of an accompanying illustration.
predicates.operative_text_is_broad_enough_to_cover_: The provision’s language does not exclude the situation described in the illustration.
predicates.statutory_illustration_covers_situation: An illustration accompanying the provision describes the situation under consideration.

issues.definition: When statutory language can cover a situation described in an accompanying illustration, the illustration may guide the construction of that language.
